chapters.title: Introduction and Three Pillars of Data Science
chapters.summary: Brandon Rohr introduces three pillars of data science: data analysis, data modeling, and data engineering.

chapters.title: Data Analysis: Domain Knowledge and Interpretation
chapters.summary: Details the components of data analysis including domain knowledge, research methods, and interpretation with visualization.

chapters.title: Data Modeling: Machine Learning Subclasses Explained
chapters.summary: Explains supervised learning, unsupervised learning, and custom algorithm development in data modeling.

chapters.title: Data Engineering: Management and Production Code
chapters.summary: Covers data management, production code deployment, and software engineering in data engineering.

chapters.title: Data Mechanics and Data Scientist Archetypes
chapters.summary: Introduces data mechanics as a fourth pillar and outlines generalist and detective data scientist archetypes.

chapters.title: Describing data science archetypes
chapters.summary: The speaker describes the Oracle archetype focused on modeling, the Maker archetype focused on engineering, and the Unicorn archetype that masters all three pillars but essentially requires stacking three careers.

chapters.title: Career planning archetypes and visualization
chapters.summary: The speaker identifies the Generalist, Detective, Oracle, and Maker as the most useful archetypes for career planning and explains a 3D plot visualization with axes for analysis, modeling, and engineering.

chapters.title: Job search advice for data scientists
chapters.summary: The speaker recommends ignoring job titles and specific tools, instead reading between the lines to identify which archetype a posting seeks and whether it matches the candidate's direction.

chapters.title: Closing advice and encouragement
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that data scientists do not need to be experts at everything, encourages choosing one direction and diving in, and wishes the audience success.
